blocks.text: Homes for sale in Port Guichon

parts.t: Port Guichon is one of the older neighbourhoods in Ladner, along the Fraser River, with character homes and quiet streets. Some parts have river views. Homes go from older heritage-style houses to updated family homes, many near the water or on older, settled streets. There are walking paths along the river and parks nearby, and Ladner’s village centre, with its shops, restaurants and services, is a few minutes away. Browse Port Guichon homes for sale below, and contact me with any questions.

Delta adopted a new Official Community Plan in 2024. Zoning and what the plan says can be different for each lot.
Delta now allows 3 units on a single detached or duplex lot up to 280 square metres and 4 units on a bigger lot. Secondary, coach and garden suites count toward those limits.
Delta has over 63 km of dikes, seawalls and shoreline protection, and expects to upgrade them as sea levels rise.

Is there an official Port Guichon boundary?
Port Guichon is both an historic BC community name and an MLS® sub-area name with map lines set by the real estate board rather than a municipal boundary bylaw, so ask me about any specific address.
What is Port Guichon known for?
A Delta plaque says that after the railway reached Port Guichon in 1903, the town took over from Ladner as Delta’s main transportation centre.
Port Guichon Elementary is at 4381 46A Street. Check the Delta School District school locator for your address.
Is Port Guichon in a flood zone?
Port Guichon is along the Fraser River, on low land behind Delta’s dikes. Ask about the exact lot’s flood rule on the title (covenant) and how high a home must be built.
